root_cause.text: persistent_ram_save_old() does not reallocate the old_log buffer when the buffer size increases between sequential calls, causing a heap buffer overflow by writing data of the larger size into the previously allocated smaller buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check to free the old buffer when `prz->old_log_size != size` before reallocating, and the commit description states: "Currently, the function only allocates prz->old_log when it is NULL, but it unconditionally updates prz->old_log_size to the current buffer size and then performs memcpy_fromio() using this new size. If the buffer size has grown since the first allocation ... this leads to: 1. A heap buffer overflow (OOB write) in the memcpy_fromio() calls".
